claims.text: The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a reported terminal strain of 13.5%.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has established impact-triggered chemical-energy-release performance.
Warm deformation at approximately 900 K will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Warm deformation will increase grain-boundary misorientation or otherwise alter grain-boundary character to favor plastic deformation.
Aging near 400 °C for one hour will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale second-phase precipitates at the grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates produced by aging will be ductile.
Refined grains and ductile grain-boundary precipitates will delay tensile crack initiation.
Refined grains and ductile grain-boundary precipitates will delay tensile crack propagation.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will increase room-temperature tensile uniform elongation to at least 20% at approximately 1×10^-4 s^-1.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength within ±10% of 786 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain compressive strength within ±10% of 1314 MPa.
The proposed treatment will retain or slightly enhance impact-triggered chemical-energy release in thin-steel-target penetration.
Overaging or precipitate coarsening could compromise the alloy's mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis uses the reported 13.5% terminal strain as the apparent reference for tensile uniform-elongation improvement, although terminal strain and tensile uniform elongation are not established as the same loading mode or metric. Consequently, the stated ≥20% uniform-elongation target and the '<15% improvement relative to baseline' falsification threshold do not share a clearly defined tensile baseline.
